claim: A paper whose entire contribution is explaining WHEN/WHY a claimed phenomenon (emergent abilities) appears -- attributing it to metric choice rather than a new method or new capability -- won the NeurIPS 2023 Outstanding Paper Award, the top honor at a top-tier ML venue.
stance_target: a 'when does X actually happen' scope/boundary-condition contribution, with no new method, can be a top-tier-venue headline contribution, not just a red flag
scope_conditions: NeurIPS 2023 main track, Outstanding Paper Award
quoted_support: we present an alternative explanation for emergent abilities: that for a particular task and model family, when analyzing fixed model outputs, emergent abilities appear due to the researcher's choice of metric rather than due to fundamental changes in model behavior with scale

claim: The paper's methodological strength is that it makes and confirms multiple falsifiable, testable predictions (on InstructGPT/GPT-3, on a BIG-Bench meta-analysis, and by deliberately manufacturing 'emergent' vision-task results via metric choice) rather than resting on a single works-here/fails-there anecdote.
stance_target: what distinguishes an accepted scope-condition paper from a rejected one -- falsifiable predictions plus mechanism, not just a contrast
scope_conditions: three complementary analyses across InstructGPT/GPT-3, BIG-Bench, and vision tasks
quoted_support: we (1) make, test and confirm three predictions on the effect of metric choice using the InstructGPT/GPT-3 family... (2) make, test and confirm two predictions about metric choices in a meta-analysis of emergent abilities on BIG-Bench; and (3) show how to choose metrics to produce seemingly emergent abilities in multiple vision tasks
